target_customer: Local businesses and e-commerce merchants needing same-day delivery
problem: Small businesses could not easily offer same-day local delivery without running couriers; Rickshaw dispatched a courier network through a web form, REST API or spreadsheet.
business_model: Per-delivery fee, from $5.50 per delivery per its site

founders.name: Gautam Jayaraman
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has worked at five YC-backed companies since 2006.

technical_complexity.rationale: Dispatch and routing software over third-party couriers, using algorithms and mobile apps. Standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: It relied on partner courier companies and had no stated exclusive supply or network effects; delivery APIs from Postmates and later Uber were similar.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: DoorDash hired the team in September 2017 as an acquihire and Rickshaw shut down, with its software applied to DoorDash Drive.

market_need_then: Delivery demand was growing: Postmates opened an on-demand API in December 2014. Rickshaw launched its API publicly in April 2015.

branding.domain_note: Used gorickshaw.com, a prefixed domain, suggesting rickshaw.com was unavailable; not stated by a source.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and merchant-friendly: tagline 'You get the customers. We get the drivers.'

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: You get the customers. We get the drivers.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered the launch and acquisition, but no sources describe brand identity or community. The name is a common word, which helps recall but not distinctiveness.

outcome_analysis: Rickshaw ran a profitable, four-person delivery API business and considered a Series A, but DoorDash hired the team in September 2017 and the service was shut down. The CEO said joining DoorDash was a natural fit. Terms were not disclosed and DoorDash's CEO called it an acquihire, so the product did not survive as a standalone outcome.
notes: Funding sources conflict: Xconomy logs a March 2014 seed with undisclosed amount, CB Insights lists about 20K over 3 rounds, Madrimasd lists 120K. All aggregator level so none recorded as rounds. Postmates entry uses a search summary of a December 2014 TechCrunch article that I did not open. The live gorickshaw.com page still shows a beta page. Divya Bhat education not found. No competitor source dated near the W14 batch was found; Postmates opened an API in December 2014 (TechCrunch, search summary, not opened) which is after founding, so it is not listed as competition at founding.
